name: Maya Dela Cruz
title: Environmental Scientist & Climate Researcher
about: Environmental scientist with 9 years of field and laboratory research experience focused on coastal ecosystems, climate adaptation, and community-based conservation. I bridge rigorous science with practical policy — translating complex environmental data into actionable recommendations for governments, NGOs, and local communities across Southeast Asia.

details: Lead a 7-person team monitoring coral bleaching events across 14 Visayan reef sites.
Developed a predictive bleaching model adopted by DENR for early-warning alerts.
Secured ₱18M in research funding from DOST and international climate foundations.
Published 6 peer-reviewed papers; cited 340+ times in the last 3 years.
Designed community-based mangrove restoration programs covering 850 ha across Palawan.
Co-authored the Sulu Sea Biodiversity Corridor management plan (2020–2030).
Trained 120+ local government unit staff in coastal vulnerability assessments.
Conducted quarterly benthic surveys across Tubbataha Reef National Park.
Managed a database of 15 years of oceanographic sensor data.
Contributed to UNESCO World Heritage Site monitoring reports.
